text: dsh-browser 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的浏览器插件，让 agent 驱动本机 Chrome 或 Edge，并将页面镜像到右侧栏。它提供网页导航、页面快照、点击与输入、截图、等待、控制台读取、JavaScript 求值和标签页管理工具。适合在 DSH 对话中查看并操作网页；需要本机安装 Chrome 或 Edge，无需 API 密钥。

dsh-browser lets a DSH Web agent drive local Chrome or Edge and mirrors the page in the right sidebar. Tools navigate, inspect, click, type, take screenshots, wait for page states, read console output, run JavaScript, and manage tabs. Requires Chrome or Edge installed locally; no API key.
想让 DSH agent 帮我打开网页并查看页面内容。
有没有办法在侧栏里实时看到 agent 正在操作的浏览器？
让 DSH 能点击网页按钮、填写表单并按键。
我想让 agent 读取网页上的可访问元素和文本，而不是只看截图。
需要给网页截长图或某个元素的图，应该怎么接入？
希望在不同 DSH 会话里分别管理浏览器标签页。
I want my DSH agent to browse and interact with pages in local Chrome.
Can I watch the browser session in a sidebar while the agent works?
dsh-browser 的功能「操作网页」：agent 可打开地址、读取页面结构、点击控件并输入文字或按键，通过网页工具完成交互。
dsh-browser 的功能「侧栏镜像」：在 DSH 右侧栏显示当前会话浏览器画面，用户可观察网页操作。
dsh-browser 的功能「截图与诊断」：保存页面截图、等待页面条件、读取控制台消息或执行 JavaScript。

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · dsh-browser：**A real Chrome or Edge for the agent to work in, mirrored in the sidebar so you can watch and take over.** Every conversation gets its own browser with its own sign-ins. It runs in both the Web and the Desktop interface.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Summary：Chrome or Edge runs as its own process, with its own profile and its own CDP port, and every conversation gets its own: tabs, sign-ins, and ports are never shared between conversations. The agent drives it, and the sidebar shows the same pages — either side can act on them.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Summary：It is not an embedded web view. The page runs in an ordinary browser process, so sites see a normal browser, DevTools or another Playwright can attach to it while the mirror is live, and closing the harness does not leave a browser pretending to be part of the app.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Highlights：- **Works in both interfaces.** The Web GUI and the Desktop app run the same plugin against the same browser; install it once in each and nothing else differs, including the settings page.
- **One browser per conversation.** Tabs, sign-ins, and ports belong to one conversation and stay there: the sidebar pane names its session, and a tool call resolves its browser from the session that called it.
- **Watch it work, or take over.** Every page the browser opens gets its own sidebar tab with a live view, and clicks and typing in that tab reach the real page.
- **The agent can read a page it has never seen.** `browser_snapshot` prints the page's accessibility tree with a `ref` per node, which is how the agent reads an unfamiliar page and how it names the element to click; `find` narrows a large page, and `boxes` gives positions without a screenshot.
- **Input a site accepts.** Real mouse and text events at the element's own position — a page that ignores a synthetic `element.click()` still takes these — plus chords such as `Ctrl+A`, native dropdowns and checkboxes, dialogs answered by the call that opens them, and an explicit refusal when somethi

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Install：Check the host dsh version first:

```sh
dsh -V
```

The published package is `@cjylzs/dsh-browser`:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @cjylzs/dsh-browser
```

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Install：| Your dsh | Plugin version | Install command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ≥ 0.1.7-rc.1 | v0.3.x (latest) | `dsh plugin --profile web add @cjylzs/dsh-browser` |
| ≥ 0.1.7-rc.1, from a tag | v0.2.x / v0.3.x | `dsh plugin --profile web add github:CJYLZS/dsh-browser#v0.3.1` |
| 0.1.5-rc.2 | v0.1.x | `dsh plugin --profile web add github:CJYLZS/dsh-browser#v0.1.0` |

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Install：The registry install takes the latest published version; a `github:` install needs the `#<tag>` ref that version pairs with, because a `github:` install without a ref takes the default branch HEAD, which drifts. The built `lib/` is committed with each tag, so a tag install needs no build step either.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Install：The profile's `package.json` records what you installed; to remove the plugin use `dsh plugin --profile web remove @cjylzs/dsh-browser`. Restart the harness after installing. A Chrome or Edge installation is required; `playwright-core` is a dependency and downloads no browser of its own.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Update：The registry install records a caret range (`^0.3.1`) and the lockfile pins the exact version that range resolved to, so re-adding the same spec is a no-op — the profile already has it. `update` is what moves within the range:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web update @cjylzs/dsh-browser
```

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Update：To pin one release instead, name it: `dsh plugin --profile web add @cjylzs/dsh-browser@0.3.0`. That records the exact version, and `update` leaves an exact pin alone — to move off one, name the range or the version you want (`…@^0.3.0`, `…@0.3.1`); re-adding the bare name changes nothing, because the profile already satisfies it. A `github:` install records the tag or commit it resolved and does not move under `update` either — re-add the spec with the ref you want, `github:CJYLZS/dsh-browser#v0.3.1`. Restart the harness afterwards in every case.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Update：Earlier releases used the unscoped name `dsh-browser`, which on npm belongs to a different project. If your profile still records `dsh-browser` (in `package.json` or `dsh.profile.bundles`), remove it with `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-browser` before adding this one: the two are separate installs, and the old key is not what the commands above touch.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Desktop：The Desktop app owns its own profile, and the ordinary CLI refuses to manage `--profile desktop` on purpose, so install through the Desktop CLI that ships with the app:

```sh
"<Desktop install dir>/resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add @cjylzs/dsh-browser
```

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Desktop：Use `<Desktop install dir>/resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh` on macOS and Linux. Restart the app afterwards, the same way the Web profile restarts after `dsh plugin --profile web add`; the same `remove` verb uninstalls it.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · From the Plugins page：Neither interface needs a terminal for this: **Plugins → Add plugin** takes the repository address with its `#<tag>` pin (the screenshot shows the bare address, and without a ref it takes the default branch HEAD), and **Install** applies it to the profile that is running — in the Desktop app that is the app's own profile, so the Desktop CLI above is not the only way in. The dialog says when the plugin waits for a restart; restart then.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Compatibility：A build targets one dsh generation, so install the plugin version that pairs with your dsh. The fork is in the client half — dsh 0.1.7-rc.1 replaced the settings model with no compatibility layer — which is why one build cannot serve both generations.

That fork is in the client half's imports, so one build cannot target both generations and the plugin pairs by generation:

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Compatibility：- **v0.2.x → dsh ≥ 0.1.7-rc.1**, declared as `peerDependencies: >=0.1.7-rc.1` with no upper bound, so one build runs on the whole 0.2.0 line it is verified against ([why the cap went away](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-09-30-peer-range-floor-only.md)). The settings page's fields are marked volatile in the schema, and an edit reaches the running browsers through `loader/volatile-update`.
- **v0.1.x → dsh 0.1.5-rc.2**, declared as `peerDependencies: ^0.1.5-rc.2`. The settings page registers a namespace scope and renders its own controls.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Compatibility：An older dsh fails loudly: dsh activates a plugin only when its dsh peers satisfy the declared ranges, and names the plugin and the unsatisfied ranges when they do not. A later generation passes that check, so whether this build still runs on one is a question for verification rather than for the version number.
@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Understand the design：The plugin keys everything by the harness session id, and that one decision explains most of its behavior:

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Understand the design：- **Two independent paths resolve the same session.** The sidebar pane is registered into a session-scoped slot, so its registration receives the session id and names it on the viewer socket; a tool call has no pane, so it takes the session from the agent executing it (`exec.agent.id`, which is the same `SessionId` the API layer resumes sessions with). Neither path can reach a browser belonging to another conversation, and a tool called with no session — a scheduled job, or a subagent without one — fails instead of landing in somebody's browser.
- **One process per profile.** Chrome locks a profile directory to a single running process, so the configured profile directory is a *parent*: the browsers of one shared unit each get a subdirectory under it, named with the harness's own id escaping. Which unit depends on `profileMode` — one per conversation in `session` mode, one per project in `workspace` mode, and `temp` keeps nothing at all — so whether sign-ins carry over is the mode's answer alone. Stated plainly, because it is the price of the isolation: in the default mode **sign-ins are not shared between conversations, and do not

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Configuration：The settings section (Settings → Browser) edits the fields below and reports what is actually running, which is not the same thing as what is configured: the banner lists every session's browser with the port, window mode, and page count it really has. A deployment without a settings provider registers nothing, and the composition entry is the whole configuration.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel` | `chrome` | Which installed browser to drive: `chrome` or `msedge`. |
| `executablePath` | empty | Explicit browser binary, for installs the channel lookup misses; overrides `channel`. |
| `headless` | `true` | Run without a window. Headless has nothing to occlude or minimize, so it is the recommended value. |
| `stealth` | `true` | Remove the two markers a Playwright-started browser carries: `navigator.webdriver` and, headless, a user agent spelled `HeadlessChrome/…`. |
| `userDataDir` | empty | Parent directory of the profiles a keeping mode resolves. Empty means that mode's default: a directory under the temporary directory for `session`, `<project>/.dsh/browser` for `workspace`. `temp` ignores it. Must be absolute. |
| `profileMode` | `temp` | Who shares a sign-in, and whether anything survives the browser: `temp` keeps nothing, `session` gives every conversation its own profile, `workspace` gives every conversation in one project the same one. |
| `debugPortMin` / `debugPortMax` | `9333` / `9400` | Window the per-session CDP ports are allocated from; each browser takes the

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Configuration：`stealth` is on by default because it was measured, not assumed: with the markers in place Google served its "unusual traffic" page three times out of three, and with them removed three times out of three searches returned results — including for a real Edge window started the same way, which is what showed the markers rather than the browser to be the deciding factor. The setting exists so the comparison can be reproduced. When a deployment needs more than markers can hide, `executablePath` accepts any Chromium binary the user supplies, including hardened builds; no third-party binary is bundled or downloaded by this plugin.
@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Configuration：-----

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `browser_navigate` | Open an address; returns the final URL, the title, and the tab list. |
| `browser_snapshot` | Read the page as roles, names, and refs (`- button "Sign in" [ref=e2]`); returns the tab list too. `find` narrows it to what matches a text or a `/regex/`, with the path to each match; `boxes` adds each element's position in viewport pixels; `target` and `depth` take one subtree to a level. |
| `browser_click` | Click the element a snapshot ref names — or one found by `role` + `name`, `text`, or `selector` when the call runs — with real mouse events at its position. `button` picks the right or middle button, `double` sends the two press-release pairs a page reads as one double click; a press the page says something else would receive is refused, and `force` sends it anyway and reports what received it. A native `<select>` and a checkbox cannot be driven by a press — the popup belongs to the browser process and its options have no box to click, and a toggled checkbox writes no attribute — so `select: ["Two"]` picks an option by its value or its visible label and `checked: true|false` sets the sta

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Tools：**An action result carries a compact list of what changed.** `changed` says the page moved (`dom`), which does not distinguish a click that opened what it named from one that only repainted a spinner. So the action also reports the **first few** changes the page made, each in facts the page itself can stand behind — its tag, the `role` it declares, and a short piece of what it says: `dom: +1 status "Saved"; ~ p "24.1k" → "24.2k"; ~ button "Save" disabled: (none) → "true"`. The list is capped at five and the changes that did not fit are **counted** rather than dropped, and every entry is structured (`kind`/`tag`/`role`/`preview`/`attribute`/`from`/`to`) so a PTC program can branch on it. This is the page's own description of itself, for knowing where to look: the accessible roles and names are still `browser_snapshot`'s to report.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Tools：**A dialog is answered by the call that opens it.** A `confirm`, `prompt`, or `alert` blocks the page until it is answered, so there is no moment at which a later call could answer one: pass `dialog: "accept"` — with `dialogText` for a prompt — on the call that triggers it, or the default dismissal is reported in the result. Every dialog is answered before the call returns and none is silent: the result names what the page asked and how it was answered, and `changed` says `dialog`, so "the page did not change" can never be the report for a click a site stopped to confirm.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Tools：The set is deliberately small because `browser_evaluate` exists: a tool earns its place only by doing something code cannot, which here means trusted input, reading a page without knowing its selectors first, and the two questions that cannot be asked after the fact — whether a state has been reached (`browser_wait`), and what the page said about itself while it failed (`browser_console`, whose listener has to be subscribed before the page's own scripts run). All three are deliberate exceptions to "new capability becomes a parameter, not a tool name" (the third is `browser_tabs`: a page is not a property of the current page, and page script cannot see another target); the screenshot's shapes are the rule followed instead: `fullPage`, an element target, and `inline` are parameters on the tool that already existed. Choosing an option and setting a checkbox are the same shape — `select` and `checked` are parameters on `browser_click` — because a press can do neither. Deliberately absent are `back`/`forward`/`reload` (the pane has reload; history is one expression), hover, drag, upload, and download — each would be added when a real case needs it, not

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Tools：Screenshots are written to a file, and the path comes back so it is durable in the session log. `inline: true` also attaches the image to the result, which costs no second call; the attachment is a reference the harness's attachment service mints (the plugin declares that service structurally and does not depend on its package), and the call is **refused before the capture** when the calling model does not declare image input — an image block is part of the tool result, so attaching one to a model that cannot read it would fail that request and every request after it.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：-----

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Dev Note：The plugin directory is a self-contained pnpm workspace (`packages: [- .]`, `storeDir: .pnpm-store`) so pnpm cannot reach the harness repository's workspace. dsh framework packages are `peerDependencies` (`>=0.1.7-rc.1`, supplied by the host profile) and pinned exactly in `devDependencies` for local types and builds.

To run a local checkout instead of a tag, link it into the profile — later `pnpm run build` runs apply on the next harness restart without re-adding:

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Dev Note：```sh
cd dsh-browser
pnpm install          # self-contained workspace; store lives in .pnpm-store/
pnpm run build        # emits lib/index.js (host) and lib/client.js (browser)
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-browser

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Dev Note：Commands: `pnpm run build` (tsdown, both halves), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm test`, and the measurement rigs in `scripts/` (`prove.mjs` for the CDP port, screen cast, input dispatch, and screenshot; `modes.mjs` for headless/windowed/minimized; `cdp.mjs` to read or drive a running browser over its external port, with `--port=` to pick a session's).

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Dev Note：`pnpm test` runs on Node's own TypeScript support (`node --test "test/**/*.test.ts"`), with no loader dependency — which is also a constraint on the source: enum, parameter properties, and other non-erasable syntax do not run. Browser-dependent behavior is tested against a recording launcher (`test/support/browser.ts`) that hands out fake pages and CDP sessions, so the suite needs no Chrome. What such fakes cannot prove — the shape of a real accessibility tree, the coordinate space of a real click, whether a real click is trusted — was verified once against Chrome and lives in the decision notes under [`.agents/notes/`](.agents/notes/README.md).
@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Dev Note：The built `lib/` is committed, so commit the rebuilt output with any source change or a GitHub install serves stale code.

@cjylzs/dsh-browser README · Third-party code：None is bundled. `lib/index.js` imports `playwright-core` (Apache-2.0) and `ws` (MIT) as runtime dependencies, and `lib/client.js` requires only the host shell's platform modules, so upstream security updates reach users through their own install rather than through this repository. The plugin ships no browser either: it drives the Chrome or Edge installation that is already on the machine, through `playwright-core`'s `channel` lookup, so the roughly 200 MB download a bundled browser would cost is not part of installing this.
